item.content:encoded:
Hmm, I don't know about this one. I kinda feel like it would have actually worked better if the religious aspects of the infection had been left in and the personality traits removed instead (and that's coming from an agnostic.) As it is, the part about the guy who contained it being a Satanist comes off as a bit of a non sequitur, especially since there's no reason to believe he didn't have any of the listed personality traits.

Also, why are violent D-class preferred for interacting with it? It seems like -a's are the least likely to spread the infection, at least if you provide them with a painless suicide method in a closed room with no other people. -B's are both inherently more dangerous and harder to control, and are able to spread the infection further with their shouting. Why would we want to have a higher chance of making that type?

I don't want to downvote this, because I do like the rest of it. Those issues, and the bit about people using it as an excuse to torture and kill their colleagues, mean I can't upvote it either, though. No vote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I mostly like this SCP, but my reasons for liking it make it implausible. Lest me explain.

I love a good puzzle SCP. I also love the genre I tend to call "speculative theology," where the story takes a religious view (usually, but not always, Abrahamic) and skews it in interesting ways. Between those 2 loves, I went at this like a rubic's cube. There's too much information. I don't have the "answer," but if this were a real life cognitohazard, I'd probably have figured out enough to self-infect.
Its a great puzzle, but in-setting, there shouldn't be enough for even the best Foundation scholars with far more relevant knowledge to figure anything out. I mean, the foundation has need of zealots of all stripes for various purposes, and some might become desperate for the answer just off of this file. Whether the key is to Heaven, Hell, Eden, or something different (I'm thinking Gnostic, maybe…), people would want to free or destroy it quite badly.
That's also ignoring the nature of the meme. Memes are information. People reading this might be forgiven for thinking "memetics" was mis-invoked, but seems like it is being used correctly. The meme label is just muddying the water. A better word (not in the article, mind you) might be evidence or Truth. So even having the slightest idea what this is makes the selfless kill (because that is presumably a kindness), and lets people … more or less apotheosize. The scarier thing may be that the meme is being contained!
Also, kudos for featuring a devout devil-worshiper (I'm assuming this wasn't Laveyan Satanism, or was some syncretic offshoot). Logically, the Foundation needs ALL types. For all the Imams, priests, shamans, devout athiests, etc. the foundation has, it also needs Pastafarians, Satanists, Hollow Earthers, Discordians, Moonies, Scientologists, and others.1
Anyway, that's a neutral vote for awesome puzzle SCP that the file should be redacted to the point of being uninterestingly "over-expunged" for in-setting reasons.

…perhaps if you hid a dangerously un-expunged version in the edit history? Nah, people wouldn't bother to look.
EDIT: Damn, that was a long and rambling post!

Footnotes
1. No insult, criticism, or doubt is intended to followers of any of these beliefs.

item.content:encoded:
I think a lot of the "memetic" SCPs are kinda "eh" anyway. The self-keeping secret one is fairly amusing, but this one seems to be memetic because Memetic Shit Is Scary. There's absolutely no reason that this couldn't be converted into a non-memetic SCP having to do with touching or handling the key, and just give the key itself some sort of alluring or compelling aura that makes it more difficult to contain. Plenty of SCPs on the site propagate themselves through such manners without going "meme memetic meme" through the whole article.

Even the meme thing might not be so bad if it were worked out more thoroughly or used more sparingly. In fact it would probably work if you went the complete opposite direction and described the key in ridiculous, exacting detail, with numerous notes about Read this carefully or we will blow your redacted head off! because it's actually the curiosity about what it is or what it looks like or what it feels like that starts the process of wanting to touch it and thus kick off the infection.

I don't know, I guess that wouldn't necessarily be communicable via conversation, just that this is very "Eh" to me. It seems like it was written with a "Memetic SCPs, huh? I will make THE most memetic of SCPs!" mindset and is not very well thought-out or compelling beyond attempting to be the Very Best Memetic SCP.

item.content:encoded:
Yeesh, this one's Flame Bait, isn't it?

Okay, looking over it objectively… I don't care for its tone as a SCP. The idea might be sound, but there's a lot of confusion arising from it, and I still have trouble making sense of it. So my downvote is for being poorly worded and constructed. This does not read like a clinical SCP.

Now, the inherent assumptions in the article are a different kettle of fish, which make it rather polarizing. Religion does not equate to spirituality, as a for instance. Atheism *is* a spiritual belief and as such people can be greatly devoted to it.

So, my opinion is that this needs a serious rewrite for tone. It needs to be more dry, to say the least. If you're afraid of spreading the effects, well that's what [DATA EXPUNGED] is for. The O5 warning on the top… yeah, not a good place. O5's have other things to do than comment on such things. Again, that falls under tone.

Sorry, dude… I don't know if it's salvageable, but I wish you luck.
